paper.title: A Theory of Fads, Fashion, Custom, and Cultural Change as Informational Cascades

headline: BHW 1992 informational cascade (agent-based): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; at p=0.7 formation-by-20=0.9998, P(incorrect|cascade)=0.1540 (closed form 0.1552), E[agents before]=3.456 (closed form 3.448)

verdicts.gate: P1 cascade forms almost surely: formation-by-agent-20 fraction >= 0.999 for all p>=0.6
P2 cascades can be WRONG: |P(incorrect|cascade) - (1-p)^2/(p^2+(1-p)^2)| <= 0.005 at p in {0.6,0.7,0.8}
P3 early onset + impaired social learning: E[agents before cascade] ~ 2/(p^2+(1-p)^2)=3.45@p=0.7, and social gain <= 0.16

extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published theoretical model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline recover the model's closed-form cascade statistics from a genuine sequential Bayesian agent-based simulation, and would catch an artifact (wrong barrier, tie-break, or precision)

citations: Bikhchandani, S., Hirshleifer, D. & Welch, I. (1992). A Theory of Fads, Fashion, Custom, and Cultural Change as Informational Cascades. Journal of Political Economy 100(5):992-1026. doi:10.1086/261849.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against the paper's closed forms (1-p)^2/(p^2+(1-p)^2) and 2/(p^2+(1-p)^2)
